gaps.criterion: Cursor pagination stable under concurrent inserts
gaps.gap: The cursor is correct by construction and asserted: it is a composite of created_at AND source_record_id, because captures arrive in bursts and two sharing a millisecond would otherwise be skipped or duplicated depending on the comparison operator; it round-trips, survives an id containing the separator, and a malformed cursor is a 400 rather than a silent restart at page one, which in a queue means re-serving rows an operator already triaged. Writing that test found a real bug - I split on the LAST separator when the timestamp is the part that cannot contain a pipe, so it must be the first. What is NOT proven is stability UNDER CONCURRENT INSERTS, which is what the criterion actually says: no test inserts rows between two page reads and asserts nothing is skipped or repeated. That needs the upstream list endpoint to accept the cursor and a live source-record store to insert into between calls - both now possible against the local gateway, which they were not when this was written.
